questions.text: A developer issues the Linux command pip3 freeze in an activated Python 3 virtual environment. What is the function that is provided by the command?
options: to output a list of installed Python packages
to lock the current virtual environment
to prepare the environment before installing a Python package
to deactivate the current virtual environment
questions.explanation: pip3 freeze prints every package installed in the active environment with its exact version (name==version) — the usual way to produce a requirements.txt. Despite the name it doesn't lock or freeze anything; deactivate is what leaves the environment.

questions.text: What are two characteristics of the Git version control system? (Choose two.)
options: It is a local VCS.
It is a centralized VCS.
It is a distributed VCS.
It is Microsoft proprietary.
It is Cisco proprietary.
It is open source.
questions.explanation: Git is an open-source, distributed VCS: every clone holds the full repository history, so there is no single central server the way there is in a centralized system.

questions.text: Match the Lean term with a description.

pairs.term: a simple statement of what a user needs and why
uses standup meetings to review progress
a time-boxed period where working software is developed
a prioritized list of all the features for the software being developed

questions.explanation: A story captures one user need and the reason for it; the backlog is the prioritised list of all of them; a sprint is the time-box in which a slice of working software gets built; and the Scrum team is who meets daily at standups to review progress. (These are really Scrum terms, which is how the course presents them.)

questions.text: What characteristic describes a formal code review?
options: Code is automatically sent for review by source code management systems once it is checked in.
The entire code base is reviewed in a series of meetings.
It utilizes a peer code review tool to identify code that needs retesting.
It provides direct interaction between the review team and the code author.
questions.explanation: A formal review walks the whole codebase line by line across a series of meetings. Automatic review on check-in is a tool-assisted review, and one-on-one interaction with the author is closer to an over-the-shoulder review.

questions.text: Which fundamental Lean principle forms the basis from which all other Lean principles flow?
options: build integrity in
eliminate waste
deliver as fast as possible
amplify learning
questions.explanation: Lean's seven principles all aim at minimising waste and maximising customer value, and eliminate waste is the one the others derive from.

questions.text: When a unified .diff file is being reviewed, which symbol is used to indicate that a line has been added?
options: /dev/null
questions.explanation: In unified diff format + marks an added line and - a removed one. @@ opens a new hunk (with the line ranges), and /dev/null stands in for the other side when a whole file was added or deleted.

questions.text: What special characters are used to enclose JSON objects?
options: forward slash /
square brackets []
curly braces {}
parentheses ()
questions.explanation: A JSON object is a set of key/value pairs wrapped in curly braces. Square brackets enclose JSON arrays, not objects.

questions.text: What are two features of the formal code review? (Choose two.)
options: For a quicker turnaround, it involves only one reviewer.
It involves the developer going through code with the reviewer line-by-line.
It promotes discussion among all of the reviewers.
It allows the developer to make changes on the spot.
It involves a review of the entire code base in a series of meetings.
questions.explanation: A formal review covers the entire codebase across a series of meetings, with discussion among all the reviewers. One reviewer sitting with the developer and changing code on the spot describes an over-the-shoulder review instead.

questions.text: Which statement describes the Waterfall methodology of software development?
options: Process tasks are broken up into time-boxed iterations called sprints.
Each step in the process must be completed before the next step starts.
It emphasizes elimination of wasted effort and maximizes customer value.
Multiple steps in the process are started simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Waterfall is strictly linear: each phase begins only when the previous one is complete. Sprints belong to Agile/Scrum and eliminating waste is Lean.

options: code that has no reviewer comments
code that has passed functional testing
code that is easy to read and understand
code that performs a discrete task
questions.explanation: Clean code is about readability: neat formatting, intuitive names, appropriate comments, and code that is reusable and easy to unit-test. Passing tests or having no review comments doesn't make code clean.

questions.text: Match the Git command with its function.

pairs.term: updates the local copy of the Git repository with the content of the remote Git repository
creates an empty Git repository or makes an existing folder a Git repository
updates the remote Git repository with the content changes from the local Git repository

questions.explanation: git init starts a repository in the current folder; git pull brings the remote's changes down into your local copy; git push sends your local commits up to the remote.

questions.text: What is the role of the view component in the Model-View-Controller (MVC) flow?
options: It accepts selected data and displays the visual representation to the user.
It accepts the input and applies the required rules to format the data.
It requests user input and manipulates it to fit the format for the model.
It manages the data, logic and rules of the application.
questions.explanation: The view is the visual representation of the data it is given. Accepting and manipulating input is the controller's job, and managing the data, logic and rules is the model's.

questions.text: A developer is constructing some functions in Python. When is a function referred to as a module in Python?
options: when the function is declared during the execution of a Python program
when the function is initiated during the execution of a Python program
when the function is packaged in a single Python file
when the function is used for the first time
questions.explanation: In Python a module is simply a .py file of packaged code (functions, classes, variables) that other code can import.

questions.text: A student is learning Python using the interactive interpreter mode. The student issues these commands. Which command should the student use to create an object with one attribute being a valid URL?
questions.context:
>>> class Url():
...     def __init__(self, host, prot):
...         self.host = host
...         self.prot = prot
...         self.url = self.prot + "://" + self.host
...
>>>
options: >>> url2 = Url(URL, 'http://', 'www.cisco.com')
>>> url2 = Url('http', '://', 'www.cisco.com')
>>> url2 = Url('www.cisco.com', 'http')
>>> url2 = Url('http', 'www.cisco.com')
questions.warning: The live question may show the class as Uri with def_init__ — read it as Url with __init__. The answer is still Url('www.cisco.com', 'http').
questions.explanation: __init__ takes host first and prot second, then builds prot + "://" + host. So Url('www.cisco.com', 'http') gives url2.url == 'http://www.cisco.com'; swapping the arguments produces 'www.cisco.com://http', and the three-argument calls raise a TypeError. Outside Source shows the class as Uri with def_init__; this was fixed to Url / __init__ so the options actually match the class, and checked by running it.

questions.text: A developer issues the Linux command python3 -m venv devenv. What is the developer trying to achieve?
options: to activate the Python 3 virtual environment named devenv
to enter the Python 3 virtual environment named venv using the devnet tool sets
to install the devnet tool sets in the Python 3 virtual environment named venv
to create a Python 3 virtual environment named devenv
questions.explanation: -m venv runs Python's built-in venv module, and the argument after it is the folder to create — so this creates an environment named devenv. Activating it is a separate step: source devenv/bin/activate.
